#2741. Who has the edge between the Patriots and Lions?

The New England Patriots had a terrible, horrible, no good, very bad day last Sunday against the Green Bay Packers. Unfortunately for them, they might have to wait a bit longer for a reprieve.

Their upcoming opponent, after all, is another one of those pesky NFC North teams. After losses to the Bears and Packers, the Patriots are now taking on the Detroit Lions on the road. Far out on the road, that is: the two teams will play one another in Munich.

How the travel element will impact the game is anybody's guess. Looking at the different units in a vacuum, however, we can see why the Lions entered Week 10 as the betting favorites.

Patriots pass offense vs. Lions pass defense: Last week's loss against the Packers once again showed that the Patriots' biggest offensive issue is their inability to hold onto the football, and it starts with Drake Maye: the third-year quarterback's three interceptions put the team on the road to defeat. A repeat performance could be disastrous again, but there is reason for optimism. The Lions are a middle-of-the-road team in interceptions, and generally have been less competitive in coverage than Green Bay: they are ranked only 27th in the league in EPA per dropback (0.178). Obviously, their ability to rush the passer is a concern especially against an offensive line that will once again field a new starting five, but if New England can give Maye time in the pocket he should be able to find openings both with his arm and — going against a defense allowing 8.5 yards per scramble — with his legs. | Edge: Patriots

Patriots pass defense vs. Lions pass offense: The Packers had their way with the Patriots pass defense last week, with just two players — Christian Watson and Matthew Golden — accounting for 335 yards and two touchdowns. Granted, Green Bay's passing offense is the most explosive in the NFL, but the Lions' combination of Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams is capable of exploiting any coverage mishaps or other insufficiencies in the New England backend as well. Add the fact that the Lions offensive line has been very good in pass blocking so far, and even more pressure will be on a secondary that was relentlessly beaten deep last week. While a repeat performance might not be on the schedule this week, until Christian Gonzalez and company show they can bounce back we cannot trust the unit to deliver against another talented opponent. | Edge: Lions

Follow every snap and discuss every decision with fellow fans on the SB Nation app.

Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android.

Patriots rushing offense vs. Lions run defense: The Lions defense has had its issues this year, but stopping the run is not particularly high up the list: from a statistical perspective, this is a fairly average unit ranked 13th in EPA per run (-0.115) and 17th in yards per attempt (4.1). While that is not exactly earth-shattering, there a two reasons we are giving the edge to the designated home team in this one. Not only have the Lions shown some significant improvement over the last month and are ranked fourth in run defense since Week 6, the Patriots are also entering the matchup potentially missing their top two running backs and, as mentioned above, facing more questions along the offensive line. | Edge: Lions

Patriots run defense vs. Lions rushing offense: The Patriots run defense has rebounded nicely from a relatively rough start to the season, and is ranked fourth in the NFL in EPA per run over the last four weeks (-0.232). However, it might be facing its toughest challenge to date this week. Standout running back Jahmyr Gibbs is one of the NFL's most productive players, and entering Week 10 with 177 rushing attempts for 847 yards and nine touchdowns to his name. His 55 first downs on the ground, meanwhile, are the most in the league. The Patriots need to bring their A-game to prevent him from going over 100 scrimmage yards for a seventh time in nine games this year, but we are not so sure about their ability to do that. | Edge: Lions

Even though they lost their regular punt returner, Tom Kennedy, to a knee injury earlier in the year and are now relying on career journeyman and ex-Patriot DeAndre Carter, in that particular area, Detroit still has one of the top overall special teams units in the NFL. The Patriots, on the other hand, have been uneven both in the form of kicker Andy Borregales and, more recently, their kickoff coverage. The law of averages favors the Lions, and so do we. | Edge: Lions

The Patriots coaching staff didn't suddenly forget how to coach last week, but it also would be naive to think Mike Vrabel's crew does not deserve any blame either. Like the team itself, its coaches are therefore also in the spotlight this week. That means not just X's and O's, but also preventing pre-snap penalties and communication lapses from happening on both sides of the ball. The same is true for making in-game adjustments and being ready for Detroit to try to exploit the issues that plagued the team last Sunday. | Edge: Lions

On paper, things are not looking particularly pretty for the Patriots. That's what happens when you get blown out in your most recent game and looked as vulnerable on defense as you have in multiple years.

Of course, that does not mean the Patriots cannot still travel back to the United States with a victory in their carry-on luggage. However, it goes without saying that it takes a significant improvement on both sides of the ball to put themselves in a winning position. And if the Packers game is any indication, that improvement coming is far from a guarantee.

#2737. Sixers, Brown have a ‘humbling' night in loss to Celtics

Sixers, Brown have a 'humbling' night in loss to Celtics originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

Whatever Jaylen Brown and the Sixers dreamed up for their first matchup against the Celtics soon flew out the window on Tuesday night.

Brown was whistled for two early fouls, the Sixers fell behind and their early-season flaws were on full display in a 123-101 loss at Xfinity Mobile Arena.

"We've just got to get better," Brown said. "Tonight was humbling. We got outplayed, out-executed. So we go back to the drawing board and get ready for the next one."

Over 26 minutes, Brown had 13 points on 4-for-9 shooting and five rebounds against the team that traded him away this summer.

As for the endless dissection of his relationship with former co-star Jayson Tatum, Brown didn't have much to add Tuesday. There was no public reconciliation, no obvious on-court animosity and generally nothing to satisfy fans hoping for some kind of fireworks on that front.

"I'm just focused on doing what's best for my team," Brown said. "Everything else … to be honest, I wasn't paying attention. But credit to Jayson; he played well tonight. Credit to the Celtics. They executed, they shot the hell out of the ball and they were the better team tonight."

Tatum scored 21 points, two of which came on a third-quarter slam over LeBron James. Paul George continued his fantastic start as a Celtic by dropping 36 points and draining six three-pointers.

The Celtics dominated from beyond the arc, shooting 22 for 49 (44.9 percent). The Sixers went just 11 for 37 (29.7 percent) on another night of underwhelming offense. The team sits 22nd in the NBA in offensive rating, 24th in three-point makes per game and 21st in three-point percentage.

"I think that we've got some guys that are obviously shooting much lower percentages than their last season or their career average — almost a handful of guys," Sixers head coach Nick Nurse said. "And I don't think it's because they're shooting fallaway, totally contested ones. I think they're shots we want them to take. So I think they'll continue to take 'em and I'm pretty sure those will even out into their career averages."

Joel Embiid is at 37 percent from the floor and 4 for 33 from three-point range (12.1 percent).

The Sixers' seven-time All-Star center got through an injury scare when he rolled his ankle late in the second quarter and hit a three early in the third. It was his first long-range make since the Sixers' home opener back on Oct. 22.

"It's a work in progress," Embiid said. "I think the biggest thing is just not thinking. I'm probably overthinking it. The rhythm of the game is different. I'm so used to having to create for myself, so it's a little bit different.

"But I think I'm slowly getting better. You could see as soon as I made a three, the next shot in the short corner … I didn't even think about it. I just shot it and let it fly, and I made it. … I think it's just about taking what's in front of you. Make or miss, keep working on your game. It's going to get there at some point."

Even with the Sixers second in the Eastern Conference standings at 9-3, Embiid believes the team's defense has "slacked off a little bit" in recent games.

"I don't really look at the record," he said. "I just look at the process of, 'Are we getting better every day?' We can always do a better job at all phases of the game."

"They're one of the top teams in the league and they've been together for a while," Brown said. "We've got a lot to work on over here, so we've got to get to work."

The Sixers will face the Raptors on Thursday night in Philadelphia.

They'll have to wait until Jan. 21 in Boston to see the Celtics again.

"I was looking forward to this," Brown said. "I was looking forward to playing well, but s— happens. Just get ready for the next one."

#2734. Observations after Sixers suffer blowout loss to Cavs, fall in NBA Cup

Observations after Sixers suffer blowout loss to Cavs, fall in NBA Cup originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

The Sixers couldn't rekindle the magic of their comeback home-opening win over the Cavaliers.

They fell Friday night in NBA Cup action, suffering a 119-95 defeat in Cleveland. The Sixers dipped to 8-2 and the Cavs improved to 5-4.

The Sixers' top scorers were Jaylen Brown (20 points), VJ Edgecombe (19 points) and Tyrese Maxey (17).

The Cavs got 23 points from Donovan Mitchell and 22 from Evan Mobley.

The Sixers' injured players included center Adem Bona (cervical spine sprain). Cleveland was down big man Jarrett Allen (right knee contusion). Sam Merrill sat out the second half with a right elbow injury.

With Friday's loss, the Sixers are 1-1 in Eastern Conference Group B of the NBA Cup. Their next Cup game is scheduled for Nov. 25 against the Heat.

The Sixers will conclude their three-road trip Sunday afternoon against the Bulls. Here are observations on their blowout loss to Cleveland:

After a missed Merrill three-pointer, the Sixers steamed ahead on the fast break and Edgecombe opened the scoring with a slam.

The Cavs replied with a 15-0 run kickstarted by six straight Mitchell points. Much like in the Sixers' Oct. 22 win over Cleveland, they were many levels below their best in the first quarter.

The Sixers began 0 for 4 from three-point range, including two LeBron James misses. The Cavs were also the better team in transition and limited the Sixers' chances to attack in the open floor by taking excellent care of the ball in the early going. Edgecombe was called for his second foul with 7:34 left in the first quarter.

Meanwhile, Joel Embiid expressed his frustration about a couple of early no-calls. Embiid's larger problem was that he couldn't hit any sort of shot besides free throws.

He went 0 for 9 from the floor in the game. The seven-time All-Star finished with six points and seven rebounds.

Embiid has had a subpar shooting start to the year, especially from three-point territory — he's now 3 for 28 (10.7 percent) — but Friday was the kind of extreme night that's bound to happen here and there over the course of a long season.

Of course, it's notable that Embiid's been playing through right foot plantar fasciitis and the Sixers have been keeping a close eye on his minutes. We'll see how the team manages his availability moving forward and whether Embiid is able to bounce back next time out.

James didn't play anywhere near his finest game either. He had eight points on 3-for-12 shooting, eight rebounds, three assists and six turnovers.

As a team, the Sixers were 36.5 percent from the field and 25 percent beyond the arc.

Jabari Walker rejoined the Sixers' rotation as the backup center with Bona sidelined. Anfernee Simons, former Cav Dean Wade and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope all remained rotation fixtures.

With Walker and Caldwell-Pope on the court next to three starters, the Sixers cut their deficit to single digits in the second quarter. Walker threw down a fast-break dunk that cut Cleveland's lead to 48-41. He gave the Sixers some good defensive possessions when switched on to James Harden and provided his usual physical, high-effort work on the glass.

Edgecombe was fantastic in the second, sinking three triples, racking up 15 points and nabbing three steals.

Many second-year players would have a tough time finding a rhythm after encountering early foul trouble, but Edgecombe was great as soon as he checked back in and delivered a ton of valuable buckets in the Sixers' comeback push.

The Sixers pulled to within 66-63 when Maxey picked a steal and threw a pretty one-handed bounce pass to Edgecombe for a dunk.

With Embiid and James offering little as scorers, Brown hit several shots that helped the Sixers stay in the game. After his 30-point performance last time out against the Pistons, Brown reached the 20-point mark for a third consecutive game.

Still, the Sixers' offense never got rolling. The Cavs maintained their lead and extended it late in the third quarter. By early in the fourth, the Sixers trailed by over 20 points.

Embiid didn't play the fourth quarter and logged 25 minutes. He's had zero made field goals on just one other occasion in his career, back in Nov. 2019 against the Raptors.

Even with their tremendous first nine games, the Sixers knew they'd hit speed bumps throughout the year. They'll try to get back on track Sunday in Chicago.

Week 10, beginning with Thursday night's game against the Washington Commanders, is a massive one for the New York Giants. What happens will tell us a great deal about how difficult the Giants' path to their first NFC East title since 2011 will be.

Team Rankings gives the 5-2-1 Giants a 69.5% chance of winning the NFC East. The 4-5 Dallas Cowboys are at 24.0%, and the 2-5-1 Commanders are at just 6.4%.

The Giants are 1.5-point favorites to beat the Commanders Thursday night, per FanDuel Sportsbook. The Cowboys host the 7-1 San Francisco 49ers, and Dallas is a 4.5-point underdog.

If the Giants win and the Cowboys lose, the NFC East standings will look like this:

The Giants will have a 3½-game lead. In that scenario, if the Giants go a reasonable 3-5 over their final eight games, they would finish 9-7-1. Dallas would have to go 6-1 to get to 10 wins, which is what they would need to win the division since the Giants' tie with the Commanders counts as half a victory.

I doubt even the most ardent of Cowboys fans would feel good about Dallas's chances of pulling that off.

If the Giants lose Thursday and Dallas upsets the 49ers, this is what the NFC East would look like:

Dallas would be just 1.5 games back, and the Commanders would be back in the hunt with eight games remaining.

The highly publicized, and now failed, Taylor trade discussions.

Missing Sunday's game against the Philadelphia Eagles, which would have marked his return to the place where he suffered his dislocated ankle in 2025.

His costly fumble against the Commanders in Week 5, which led to his pseudo-benching in Week 6.

#2730. Back in Philadelphia with Celtics, Paul George looks forward to ‘a regular game'

Back in Philadelphia with Celtics, Paul George looks forward to 'a regular game' originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

Paul George's presence back in town was one of the many swirling morning storylines at Xfinity Mobile Arena.

For good reason, former Celtics teammates Jaylen Brown and Jayson Tatum will draw immense attention Tuesday night. After all, Brown has said there "might be a little lamb chops with some gravy" between the two, if not a full-blown beef.

But George's return to Philadelphia is more than a tiny subplot. Following two seasons in Philadelphia, he was the centerpiece of the Sixers' summer trade package to acquire Brown.

George told reporters before the Celtics' shootaround that it feels like "a regular game."

"Had I been here eight, nine, 10 years, different story," he said. "I was here two years. Obviously, we didn't have the best of luck or had a great, I think, partnership in terms of my ability to stay healthy and on the floor. So that kind of played into a lot of it.

"But obviously, it's a tremendous fan base, a great sports town to play in. So that was appreciated. There's no ill will for me. It'll be fun to just compete. And outside of that, it's a normal game."

The 36-year-old George indeed had trouble staying available for sustained stretches as a Sixer. He dealt with a variety of injuries and served a 25-game suspension last season for violating the NBA's anti-drug policy.

George did play well on both ends of the floor for much of the 2026 playoffs. He helped the Sixers come back to win a seven-game first-round series against the Celtics in historic fashion. The nine-time All-Star also brought a veteran steadiness to the Sixers' locker room and was glad to mentor younger players like VJ Edgecombe.

"Just his routine … even when he got hot, he didn't try to force it," Jabari Walker said Tuesday morning. "His game was smooth and I think that's how he is as a person, just not forcing anything and having a calm energy."

George has certainly enjoyed his early days as a Celtic.

Through nine games, he's averaged 20.4 points, 5.2 rebounds, 4.1 assists and 2.3 steals while shooting 42.5 percent from three-point range. Boston will enter Tuesday night's matchup second in the Eastern Conference standings at 8-2, the Sixers first at 9-2.

"I've been kind of blown away," George said. "I think it exceeded my expectations since being in Boston. You never know how much culture is involved and how much culture changes your outlook on things and the effect it has mentally, physically, just being in an environment … and the culture that Boston presents.

"So I've been thrilled. I've been playing some of my best basketball of late, and just been enjoying grinding it out with these guys out here. It's a fun style of play and I can't talk (enough) about just the thrill, the happiness and the excitement and joy that it has brought being here."

He was asked what sort of reception he expects from Sixers fans.

"Not sure," George said. "In some ways, I helped land them a future piece for them. So with that, not sure how the reception would be."

#2727. ‘Let's check the ball up': Jaylen Brown ready for first game against Celtics

'Let's check the ball up': Jaylen Brown ready for first game against Celtics originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

Jaylen Brown was asked Sunday whether he and Jayson Tatum had spoken since the former teammates addressed their relationship during the preseason.

Does he plan to approach Tatum before Tuesday night's game at Xfinity Mobile Arena?

"I mean, he's on his side, I'm on my side," Brown said. "We're playing basketball. Both of us are trying to win. So it's nothing to talk about. Let's check the ball up."

After months of public comments, documentaries and questions about how their partnership ended, the basketball will finally take over.

Brown will face Boston for the first time since the Celtics traded him to Philadelphia for Paul George and four future draft assets in July. He spent his first 10 NBA seasons in Boston, played nine alongside Tatum and helped the Celtics win the 2024 championship, earning Finals MVP honors.

Tuesday's 8 p.m. game on NBC will also bring together the top two teams in the Eastern Conference. The Sixers are 9-2. Boston, riding a three-game winning streak, is 8-2 and sits a half-game behind Philadelphia.

"Another good opportunity for our team to be able to show what we're made of," Brown said. "I'm looking forward to it. Big-time matchup, two heavyweights in the East. Let's get it."

Brown has not hidden his appreciation for Boston, even as more has emerged about the deterioration of his relationship with Tatum and the organization.

"I love Boston," he said Sunday. "Boston's a great city. A lot of people I developed relationships with, you know what I mean? But I'm just focused on what's in front of me right now. And that's the most important thing."

He also acknowledged everything that accompanies an abrupt end to a decade with one organization.

"Decisions were made," Brown said. "It's life. It's business. Move on. It's OK. … It's emotions. You've got to pack up and move your stuff. Your family's got to pack up and move. But it's life. It's happened to numerous amounts of people, myself included.

"So I just look forward to being able to build with my team over here, trying to make the best of my situation."

Brown faced the Celtics during the preseason, but Tuesday will be the first meeting that counts. He said he did not know whether that would introduce emotions that were absent during the exhibition schedule.

"We'll see how I feel when we get out there," Brown said. "As of now, I've got no emotion toward nothing. So I'm just ready to go."

Tatum was similarly restrained after Boston's 117-97 victory over Milwaukee on Sunday.

"It's another game on the schedule," Tatum said. "It's the Celtics versus the Sixers. In the words of Brad Stevens, they all count as one."

Tatum called the Sixers "an incredible group" with a "great coaching staff," but declined to add to the discussion surrounding his relationship with Brown.

"Drama gets clicks and views," he said. "That's not my thing." CBS Sports reported Tatum's full comments Sunday night.

Celtics head coach Joe Mazzulla was even more concise.

"It'll be fun," Mazzulla said. "It'll be a good atmosphere."

Brown is not the only centerpiece of the July deal who will face his former team.

George has settled quickly into Boston's lineup, averaging 20.4 points and supplying the high-volume outside shooting the Celtics have long prioritized. He scored 27 points and made five three-pointers Sunday as Boston beat Milwaukee for its third consecutive victory.

The Celtics have not needed George to duplicate everything Brown provided. He has fit alongside Tatum, Derrick White and Boston's returning core as another willing shooter and versatile defender.

Tatum is averaging 27.1 points, six rebounds and 7.8 assists. His playmaking has been especially important for a team that replaced Brown's downhill pressure with more shooting and ball movement.

Boston enters Tuesday ranked third in offensive rating and fourth in defensive rating. It is one of two NBA teams currently inside the top five on both ends of the floor.

The Celtics have also made 15.6 three-pointers per game, the second-highest average in the league. They set an NBA Cup record by hitting 24 against Charlotte on Friday, then made 18 more Sunday in Milwaukee.

That presents a clear challenge for a Sixers defense that has generally performed well but has occasionally surrendered clean perimeter looks after committing extra help toward the ball. Tatum, George, White, Payton Pritchard and Sam Hauser can all punish late rotations.

The Sixers have reached 9-2 without depending upon the same formula every night.

Tyrese Maxey leads them at 26.9 points per game. Brown is averaging 22.3 points, 6.7 rebounds and four assists while shooting 47.7 percent from the field and 39.2 percent from three. Joel Embiid and LeBron James have supplied scoring, passing and defensive flexibility around them.

Brown has repeatedly described the team as unfinished despite its record.

"From our perspective, it's been some growing pains for sure, even though we've been able to win," he said. "The result, we're not so much fixated on the result. It's more so about the process, and we've got to improve our process and our mentality to creating a winning environment."

Boston should provide the clearest early measure of that process.

The Celtics play considerably slower than the Sixers, but their half-court execution has been more efficient. Philadelphia will want to create turnovers and run before Boston can set its defense. The Celtics will attempt to control the pace, generate three-pointers and make the Sixers execute against a defense that has yet to allow an opposing player to score 30 points this season.

There is also the unavoidable Brown matchup. Boston could use Tatum, George and White against him at different points, giving the Celtics several defenders capable of absorbing his drives without immediately sending help.

Nick Nurse expects Brown to bring something extra, even if Brown has publicly downplayed the emotional component.

"It's going to be very different for him," Nurse said. "I think probably a little bit of emotion in there, too, but also I think he's going to be very motivated to play."

Boston's rotation is healthy entering the matchup. Two-way guard Devin Carter is out because of an illness.

Dominick Barlow and Ariel Hukporti remain out for the Sixers. Adem Bona could return after missing Sunday's contest.

The betting market views the matchup as essentially a toss-up. Monday afternoon listings had the spread moving between Boston minus-1.5 and Philadelphia minus-1.5, depending on the sportsbook, with the total at 215.5.

That fits the larger picture. Philadelphia owns the East's best record. Boston has the conference's strongest point differential and has outscored opponents by 10.7 points per game.

The surrounding conversation will center on Brown and Tatum until the opening tip. Brown does not intend to contribute any ceremonial small talk.

"He's on his side," Brown said. "I'm on my side."

#2725. Broncos' deal for Chargers LB Daiyan Henley falls through after NFL trade deadline

The Denver Broncos appeared to fill an immediate need with a trade for Los Angeles Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley. That deal is no longer happening.

Denver announced in a statement late Wednesday night that the deal, which would have seen the Chargers receive a 2027 fourth-round draft pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick, was no longer happening. No reason was provided initially.

"The proposed trade involving Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley will not be finalized. We have great respect for Daiyan as a player and person, and we wish him all the best moving forward."

It was reported Thursday that the deal was called off due to a "failed physical," per NFL Network. It's unclear what caused Henley to fail the Broncos' exam.

The development means Henley will remain with the Chargers, the only winless team in the NFL at 0-8. The deal was going to be a rental for the Broncos as Henley is a pending free agent, but the former third-round draft pick will now spend the remainder of the final year of his rookie contract in Los Angeles.

Henley has a salary of $3.7 million this season, per OverTheCap.

The Broncos, who have won five straight games, approached Tuesday's trade deadline in need of additional depth at linebacker and appeared to get that in the 27-year-old Henley, who leads the Chargers with 51 combined tackles as well as two passes defended, a forced fumble, an interception and a half sack in eight games this season.

Denver's defense ranks 10th in points allowed and 26th in total yards, while also playing more snaps than any unit in the NFL at 648. Veteran inside linebacker Alex Singleton has played 647 of those, making him the most-used defensive player in the league, and fellow inside linebacker Justin Strnad isn't far behind him at 529 snaps.

Henley would have helped give that pair some rest as a rotational option, but the Broncos will have to figure that situation out without the help of the trade deadline.

#2724. Must Cs: Celtics complete 7-point possession during 16-0 run in Toronto

On the second night of a back-to-back and without Paul George (illness), the Celtics fell into a trap game with home just a puddle jump away after a four-game road trip. After the high of Tuesday night's blowout of the 76ers and arriving in Toronto at 4 am, Boston found themselves behind the 8-ball early in the game facing a 22-point deficit midway through the second quarter.

This slick fastbreak capped off the 16-0 run in two and a half minutes.

In the end, the Celtics completed their second largest comeback in Joe Mazzulla's tenure as head coach. Down six with five minutes to go, Boston closed with a 13-4 run with some lockdown defense, gritty play on both sides of the ball from Neemias Queta, and Tatum getting to the line. However, it was that first half stretch that really made the difference in sweeping their road trip.

"His energy just lifted everybody," Mazzulla said of Tatum's presence during that crucial run. "It's the same thing when you lose close games. We didn't win the game in the fourth quarter. We won the game in the middle of the second quarter when we cut it to seven again."

#2723. Real Madrid’s Santiago Bernabeu emerges as potential host for 2027 Nations League final – report

Spain's bid to host the 2027 UEFA Nations League Final Four could give Real Madrid's Santiago Bernabeu a chance to host a major international event, with Valladolid's Jose Zorrilla Stadium also included in the proposed arrangement.

Spanish journalist Alfredo Martinez has reported through Defensa Central that UEFA is expected to favour the Spanish venues after considering other potential host countries, although it is crucial to note that the governing body has yet to announce its decision.

The Royal Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) has formally submitted its hosting proposal, with Real Madrid and Real Valladolid involved in the preparations.

The timing is significant for the Bernabeu, as Real Madrid are increasingly positioning themselves as a venue for major international sporting events ahead of the 2030 FIFA World Cup.

RFEF president Rafael Louzan confirmed on September 27 that Spain had submitted its application to host the tournament's decisive stage.

Santiago Bernabeu could host the 2027 Nations League final. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images)

The proposed venues are the Santiago Bernabeu in Madrid and Jose Zorrilla in Valladolid, with the Bernabeu expected to stage the final if Spain's bid succeeds.

Martinez explained the proposed arrangement: "The country has applied to host the tournament, and if the Spanish national team qualifies, they would normally be granted the opportunity.

"Furthermore, the other teams that could qualify have already hosted this phase in recent times: Italy, France, Portugal, and Germany. Therefore, Valladolid (Jose Zorrilla Stadium) and Madrid (Santiago Bernabeu Stadium) would be the venues for those matches."

Spain currently lead Nations League Group A3 with 12 points from four matches, having won all four of their opening fixtures.

They have already secured a place in the quarter-finals, but must still finish the group stage strongly to confirm their final position.

Real Madrid are also pushing to host the 2030 FIFA World Cup final. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images)

Hosting the Final Four would give the national team an opportunity to compete for another international trophy after winning the World Cup earlier this year.

However, the hosting decision and Spain's eventual qualification for the final tournament remain separate matters.

For Real Madrid, the proposed Nations League hosting arrangement carries significance much beyond the competition itself.

This is because Spain is also campaigning to stage the 2030 FIFA World Cup final, and the Bernabeu is an obvious candidate given its capacity and international profile, although Barcelona's Spotify Camp Nou is also in the running.

Indeed, hosting the Nations League final would not guarantee the Bernabeu the 2030 World Cup final, which remains a separate FIFA decision, although it is equally true that this competition could also strengthen the stadium's international credentials.

#2722. Rockets snag 115-108 win over shorthanded Warriors

The Houston Rockets will always take a victory over the Golden State Warriors, even when the Dubs are shorthanded, and that's exactly what happened on Wednesday night. Stephen Curry went down in the first quarter and did not return, setting the table for a Rockets victory. And while Houston did make it much closer than it needed to be, the Dubs didn't quite have the firepower without Steph to hang with the Rockets down the stretch, and despite a couple close Q4 -pushes by Golden State, the Rockets walked away with a 115-108 victory to move to 9-3 on the season.

The Rockets were led by Kevin Durant with 20 points, as all five Houston starters finished in double in figures. KD also had 4 rebounds and 5 assists. Alperen Sengun was near-miss on a triple double, finishing with 19 points, 13 rebounds, and 9 assists while shooting 8-for-14 from the field. Houston also got 19 from Amen Thompson, who finally had a decent offensive game, shooting 8-for-11. He also added 7 rebounds, 4 assists, a steal and 2 blocks for the kind of all-around performance we've been missing from Amen. Houston also 18 points and 6 assists from Fed VanVleet and 14 points and 8 rebounds from Jabari Smith Jr. to round out the scoring from the starters.

Reed Sheppard pitched in 13 points off the bench on 3-for-6 shooting from deep, and that about ended the bench contributions, as Tari Eason shot just 2-for-11, while Marcus Smart was ejected in the third quarter for throwing a punch. Welcome to the Houston-Golden State rivalry, Marcus. It took all of one half of a game for Smart to want to smack a Dub around. Sheppard had a solid fourth quarter in taking over Smart's minutes.

Houston shot 51 percent in this one, while holding the Warriors to just 41 percent. The Rockets were also hammering the ball inside, as they led in paint scoring 50-34. One of thew few reasons the game was close was the difference in three-point shooting, as Golden State put up 51 threes (making 17) to Houston's 36 attempts (making 13). The Rockets have increased their three attempts so far this season, up to 34.2 per game from 31.5. Accuracy has also increased, up to 37.5 percent from 36.4 perccent. All of that is good. But the Rockets can still find themselves in closer than needed situations when they play teams with a big three-point attempt difference.

Nonetheless, every good NBA season requires a little luck, and I'm certainly not one to feel bad about a Warriors player getting injured against the Rockets, considering the history these two teams have. I'll take the win, and we'll see you again later.

Houston's 9-3 record has moved them back up to third in the Western Conference. They will be back in action on Friday night, with a home game against another historic rival, the Utah Jazz.

As fantasy managers push past the halfway point of the NFL regular season, roster decisions often come down to high-stakes divisional clashes and volume-driven matchups. This week, we're looking at an intriguing NFC North Start 'Em, Sit 'Em debate between newly acquired Minnesota Vikings veteran Kirk Cousins and New York Giants QB J.J. McCarthy.

Let's dive into their current trends, recent play, matchups, and what fantasy football managers can expect as they weigh these two signal-callers for Week 10 lineups.

Oct 23, 2023; Minneapolis, Minnesota, USA; Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kirk Cousins (8) signals his team against the San Francisco 49ers in the third quarter at U.S. Bank Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Brad Rempel-USA TODAY Sports | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Connect

Oct 8, 2023; Minneapolis, Minnesota, USA; Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kirk Cousins (8) throws a pass during the first quarter against the Kansas City Chiefs at U.S. Bank Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jeffrey Becker-USA TODAY Sports | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Connect

Even in a tough divisional matchup against Green Bay, his offensive scheme and weapons provide a much higher floor than McCarthy's limited ceiling.

#2719. For the Wizards, it’s not as early as we think.

Okay, now I'm worried. The Wizards went to Indiana and got thumped by a Tyrese Haliburton-less Pacers team. It's Washington's fifth straight loss — and four of the five have been by 10 points or more.

If you want to stick to the "it's early" and "they're finding their way and they'll improve as the season goes on" talking points, you'll probably want to skip a few paragraphs. Because I did some looking up and some numbers crunching, and…well…it's not as early as you think. I mean, I was getting nervous when the streak reached three, and I was reciting those Talking Points myself, so let me be clear — it's not as early as I was thinking.

Wizards guard Tre Johnson played one of his better games of the season in the team's loss to the Indiana Pacers. | NBAE via Getty Images

The Wizards entered last night's game against the Pacers with a strength of schedule adjusted scoring -11.3 through 11 games. They lost by 13 to a team scoring a -6.3 in the same metric. That's not good. And the team's performance a dozen games into the season is greater cause for worry than I'd imagined.

While it feels early, analysis of NBA history says that by this point in the season, we already have about half the information needed to determine a team's relative strength in the league. Even just 8-10 games is enough to be more than just random noise.

There's still some noise — early-season blowouts have bigger impacts on this type of scoring differential metric than it will by the end of the season — but what we see in the first month of the season is a surprisingly good indicator of what we're going to see over the final five.

In the case of the Wizards this season, they may not really be the quality of a team that wins just 14-15 games (which is what their adjusted scoring margin implies), but a) they could be, and b) it's pretty unlikely they're even the quality of a 35-win team. Best case at this point is probably mid-20s in wins — better than last season, though not the major step forward many hoped.

While it's not as early as we think, it's getting later fast. We already have half the information needed to draw a meaningful conclusion. By game 20, it'll be about 70%. By game 30, it's closing in on 80%.

Perhaps the biggest wildcard in all this is the role of three-point shooting luck. According to research published on the Above the Break Substack, it takes about 33 games for opponent three-point shooting to stabilize. Unfortunately, opponent three-point shooting reverting to the mean could be brutal for Washington — so far this season opponents have been laying bricks from deep.

Of course, reversion could also benefit the Wizards on offense — they've been shooting slightly worse from the arc than their opponents. The likely outcome is reversion effects cancel each other out, and Washington ends up basically where they are now, albeit looking a bit better on offense and a bit worse on defense.

None of this is writ in stone, of course. There are examples of teams in NBA history that overcame a rough first month to become good. But it's rare. And usually those teams aren't as deep in the scoring margin hole as the Wizards are. I mean, the Sacramento Kings have been a 1-9 horror show this season, and their adjusted scoring margin is better than Washington's.

Now, it's not all doom and gloom. The Wizards rank 26th in adjusted scoring margin, but the four teams even worse are all in the Eastern Conference. It's conceivable that the Wizards could continue playing just as bad and still make the play-in thanks to the struggles of the Brooklyn Nets, Milwaukee Bucks, Charlotte Hornets, and Chicago Bulls.

The Pacers announced that Haliburton — the team's best player — will miss at least another 10 days with his hamstring injury. He's been one of my favorite watches since he entered the NBA, and he looked fantastic in his first four games back from the Achilles injury.

On a first quarter drive, AJ Dybantsa made Kelly Oubre Jr. — known for his athleticism — look slow. Oubre actually looked startled at how sudden Dybantsa was.

A first quarter sequence underscored how much work Tre Johnson needs to do on his body and his overall game. T.J. McConnell wrecked a Washington possession by denying Johnson the ball. The denial forced Davis to handle out top. After setting a half-hearted screen for Davis, Johnson kinda stood around waiting. Davis tried to throw the ball to him, McConnell stole the pass — I mean, HE WAS STANDING IN THE PASSING LANE — and then led the fastbreak, which resulted in a wide open three for Obi Toppin.

That play aside, Johnson played one of his better games of the season. One play design I liked — early in the the second quarter, the Wizards screened for him in the weakside corner. It looked kind of like a traditional pindown action, except Johnson came to the ball for a dribble handoff that gave him a wide open three-point attempt. He missed, but the design and execution was good.

Two thoroughly disgusting defensive plays in the second quarter: On the first, Oubre got a dunk because Bub Carrington turned his back on him to watch a drive on the opposite side of the floor. Oubre noticed the turned head and cut behind him for the slam. On the second, Oubre got another dunk because Young tried to cheat the screen on a sideline out of bounds play — guessing that Oubre would come off the screens towards the ball. Oubre went weak side and was wide open.

Learning moment for Dybantsa — he dribbled too high while trying to back down Oubre and got picked clean for a breakaway dunk.

If all you look at is The Glory Stats, Kyshawn George looks really good last night — 25 points, 9 rebound, 3 assists. Heck, he even shot 5-8 from three-point range. So why does he end up with a below-average score in my PPA metric? He shot 4-12 on twos, committed six turnovers, and contributed to a worse-than-average team defense.

Below are the four factors that decide wins and losses in basketball — shooting (efg), rebounding (offensive rebounds), ball handling (turnovers), fouling (free throws made).

eFG% (effective field goal percentage, which accounts for the three-point shot)

TOV% (turnover percentage — turnovers divided by possessions)

FTM/FGA (free throws made divided by field goal attempts)

PPA is my overall production metric, which credits players for things they do that help a team win (scoring, rebounding, playmaking, defending) and dings them for things that hurt (missed shots, turnovers, bad defense, fouls).

PPA is a per possession metric designed for larger data sets. In small sample sizes, the numbers can get weird. In PPA, 100 is average, higher is better and replacement level is 45. For a single game, replacement level isn't much use, and I reiterate the caution about small samples sometimes producing weird results.

POSS is the number of possessions each player was on the floor in this game.

ORTG = offensive rating, which is points produced per individual possessions x 100. League average so far this season is listed in the Four Factors table above. Points produced is not the same as points scored. It includes the value of assists and offensive rebounds, as well as sharing credit when receiving an assist.

USG = offensive usage rate. Average is 20%. Median last season was 17.7%.

ORTG and USG are versions of stats created by former Wizards assistant coach Dean Oliver and modified by me. ORTG is an efficiency measure that accounts for the value of shooting, offensive rebounds, assists and turnovers. USG includes shooting from the floor and free throw line, offensive rebounds, assists and turnovers.

+PTS = "Plus Points" is a measure of the points gained or lost by each player based on their efficiency in this game compared to league average efficiency on the same number of possessions. A player with an offensive rating (points produced per possession x 100) of 100 who uses 20 possessions would produce 20 points. If the league average efficiency is 115, the league — on average — would produced 23.0 points in the same 20 possessions. So, the player in this hypothetical would have a +PTS score of -3.0.

Players are sorted by total production in the game.

#2717. Alexander Ovechkin announces this will be his last NHL season: 'Let's have fun'

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Alex Ovechkin's 22nd NHL season will be his last, the Washington Capitals superstar announced on Monday."This is gonna be my last year," Ovechkin told his teammates in a video the Capitals posted to social media. "It's sad, but it is what it is. We have an unbelievable team this year. There are 82 games left. Let's make the playoffs, and let's have fun."

Ovechkin has already established himself as the greatest goal-scorer in hockey history with 929 tallies, and he still has 82 games to add to that total before he hangs up his skates.

The No. 1 overall pick in the 2004 NHL Draft, Ovechkin immediately established himself as a prolific scorer by notching 52 goals en route to winning the Calder Trophy as a rookie.

Since then, Ovechkin has won the Rocket Richard Trophy as the NHL's leading goal-scorer a record nine times. The Capitals legend's resume also features an Art Ross Trophy and three Hart Trophy wins.

The crowning achievement in Ovechkin's illustrious career is leading Washington to its first Stanley Cup in 2017-18. After coming up short in a number of postseasons prior to that, Ovechkin led all playoff performers with 15 goals and won the Conn Smythe Trophy as a result.

Following the 2025-26 season, there was speculation that Ovechkin could retire, but he signed an incentive-laden one-year deal with the Caps.Sensing that this could be Ovechkin's final season, the Capitals loaded up to give their franchise icon one more shot at the Stanley Cup. Washington signed former Buffalo Sabres winger Alex Tuch in free agency and acquired winger Jordan Kyrou from the St. Louis Blues via trade.

No team is as loaded on the wings as the Capitals, and they have one of the best rosters in the Metro Division. Washington has the ingredients to challenge the defending Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes and get Ovechkin one more ring before he rides off into the sunset.

#2715. Sixers look to move past loss to Boston as they host Raptors

Despite sitting at a highly respectable 9-3 and featuring the star-studded starting five that had everyone doing backflips over the offseason, concerns are emanating around the Philadelphia 76ers. It's amazing what getting smacked around for the final quarter and a half against the Celtics will do to a team's vibes. Tuesday night also marked the Sixers' second 20-plus-point loss in their last three games, which doesn't overly inspire confidence.

I think it's important to remember for those suddenly down on the Sixers or ready to crown Boston that nothing is won in early November. Still, there are areas for improvement on both ends of the court for Philadelphia. The offense has struggled, sitting just 20th in the league in offensive rating as of this writing, taking on far too much of an iso-heavy look for my liking. It would also help for Joel Embiid to rediscover his shooting stroke, currently shooting just 37.0 percent from the field on the season. However, both Embiid (plantar fasciitis) and LeBron James (lower back) are listed as questionable on the injury report for tonight's contest against the Toronto Raptors. It's worrisome that those guys are listed as questionable when it's not even a back-to-back for the Sixers. Already without Adem Bona and Dominick Barlow (and Ariel Hukporti out for the season), the Sixers could be dangerously thin in the front court.

On the other side of the ball, the Sixers have been better than most expected on that side of the ball (8th in the league in defensive rating). The consistent failure to identify and close out on open shooters against Boston certainly raised some eyebrows, however. The rebounding has also been an issue when Embiid is on the bench, which could be a big problem if he's unable to go tonight.

By and large, though, they should have an easier time of things against Toronto, who have been around a league-average team thus far this season, but are at a schedule disadvantage after hosting Boston last night, a close 98-93 defeat in which the Raptors' offense went cold in the fourth quarter. While the Sixers' injury report could definitely be better, the Raptors are dealing with their own injury concerns. Kawhi Leonard is currently out while undergoing the reconditioning process for his knee. Scottie Barnes hasn't played since November 4 due to a groin injury. Reserve forward Trayce Jackson-Davis missed last night's game due to illness. In the absence of the two big stars, six Raptors scored between 11 and 17 points last night.

Tonight is unquestionably a good spot for the Sixers, facing a team traveling on the tail end of a back-to-back and missing their best two players. Still, if Philadelphia does end up missing two key starters of their own, victory will be far from assured. The remaining stars will need to pick up the scoring slack, most notably Tyrese Maxey and Jaylen Brown. Key reserves like Dean Wade and Jabari Walker will have to assume more of the burden on the boards in expanded roles. On the other hand, perhaps the starters are all able to suit up and the Sixers are able to earn that elusive comfortable win this season. Tune in tonight to find out.

When: Thursday, November 12, 7:00 p.m. ETWhere: Xfinity Mobile Arena, Philadelphia, PAWatch: NBC Sports PhiladelphiaRadio: 97.5 The FanaticFollow: @LibertyBallers

The discussion then turned to whether the NFC East offered Dallas a realistic route into the postseason. The division's shortcomings were acknowledged, but Jason saw the Giants as a sticking point.

"I understand the NFC East is not everything it's cracked up to be. I do not think they're going to beat the Giants," Jason said. "Their defense is bad, bad… They almost lost to the Colts, who are admittedly foregoing the season."

The honeymoon is over for the Gophers in NYC as both JMS and Tyler Nubin have lost their playing time. Antoine Winfield Jr is hurt again, and Blake Cashman just keeps playing his heart out even as the Vikings offense stinks. But Max Brosmer got in the game and did well….so that's a win? Here is how the former Gophers did in Week 9 and a look ahead to Week 10.

Gibbons played 49 defensive snaps and six on special teams in the Cardinals loss to Seattle. He recorded four tackles, two of them solo. He was targeted once in the passing game and gave up one reception for 16 yards.

Bateman played 35 snaps in the Ravens loss to Jacksonville. He was targeted twice and made one catch for 6 yards.

Mafe played 50 defensive snaps in the win over the Falcons in Spain. He had three tackles, one of them solo.

Span-Ford played 55 snaps on offense and another 16 on special teams as Dallas defeated Indianapolis. He was targeted three times making a pair of catches for 20 yards. He also added a solo special teams tackle.

St. Juste got into the Packers blowout win and played 12 defensive snaps and 19 more on special teams. He made one tackle.

Ersery played all 70 offensive snaps and 8 more o special teams in the Texans win. The team did not allow a sack in the game.

Walley was inactive for the second straight week with a knee injury.

Faalele played seven special teams snaps.

Striggow played 19 defensive snaps and six on special teams in the win over Baltimore. He recorded three tackles, one of them solo and added a QB hit. He may see his playing time decrease with the Jags adding Jordan Davis from Philly before the trade deadline on Tuesday.

Lindenberg played 18 special teams snaps in the loss to San Francisco. He made one tackle.

Brosmer entered the game in the fourth quarter making his season debut. He entered to loud applause and went 6-7 for 68 yards and was sacked once as the rest of the Vikings offense was putrid in the loss to the Bills.

Cashman played 69 defensive snaps in the Vikings loss to Buffalo. He led the Vikings with 12 tackles, six of them solo and one for a loss. He added a pair of pass defenses as well.

Howden played 24 defensive snaps and 28 on special teams in the Saints OT win after Cleveland went for 2 and the win and failed the conversion. He had one solo tackle.

Schmitz still lost his job after the bye as he was dressed but did not play a snap in the Giants win over the Eagles.

Nubin also has not regained his job as he played 23 special teams snaps and not a single defensive snap in the win. He picked up a pair of special teams tackles, one of them solo.

Eastern remained on the practice squad and did not play.

Kallerup played a season high 27 offensive snaps and three special teams snaps in the win over Arizona. He did not record a stat.

Kieft played one offensive snap and 12 special teams snaps in the loss to the Bears. He had one tackle.

Winfield played just 29 snaps before leaving the game in the third quarter with an ankle injury. Before he left he recorded four tackles, two of them solo and a pass defense.

#2710. 10 Takeaways from a chaotic Celtics win over Raptors

At the 5:24 mark of the second quarter, the Boston Celtics were down 22 points to the Toronto Raptors and this looked like it was going to be a long night. The Celtics had every excuse to just roll over and die after going down big. It was the last game of a four-game road trip, the second half of a back-to-back where the first game was an emotionally draining battle against the Philadelphia 76ers, and Paul George was ruled out with an illness.

The Celtics could have chalked this game up as a loss but decided to fight, going on a ridiculous 34-8 run from the 5:10 mark of the second quarter to the 3:43 mark of the third quarter. This is the second biggest comeback in the Joe Mazzulla Era of the Celtics, with the only bigger one being a 26-point comeback against the 76ers on February 2nd last year.

This was some incredible determination by Boston and a big win going into a three-day break. Boston is now 10-2 for the first time since the 2024 season when they won the championship. Ironically, the 10th win of that season was also on the road against the Toronto Raptors.

The biggest reason why the Boston Celtics were able to get back into this game was because of an incredible performance by Jayson Tatum. If you look at the box score and see Tatum finished shooting 6-21 from the field and 2-11 from three, you might think it was a bad game. However, it was the 24 points, 8 assists, 7 rebounds, and 2 blocks as a +9 that spoke the loudest and they were the difference maker in this game.

The second quarter was the biggest impact made on the team, finishing with 11 points that all came on a personal 11-0 run. It was at this point where he single handedly told the team that they were not going to roll over.

Tatum came back into the game at the 7:28 mark of the second quarter when Boston was down 50-35. He started his run two minutes later with a three, 2 free throws and a monster slam to force Toronto into a timeout. That didn't stop Tatum, as he hit an and-1 three with a flagrant foul free throw and then found Baylor Scheierman for a three that capped off a ridiculous 7-point possession.

This run of play was followed by an ice cold stretch of 8 straight misses for Tatum, including an 0-5 third quarter, but his presence on the court kept Boston in the game. When it was clutch time in the fourth quarter however, Tatum did what he did best, hitting a huge mid range jumper over RJ Barrett to give the Celtics a one point lead with 1:55 to go.

This was not necessarily the best game that Tatum has ever played, saying postgame, "I played like sh*t all game, especially in the second half. So I just kind of wanted to do my part." But a win is a win, and Boston wouldn't have made this comeback without the impressive play of Jayson Tatum.

The biggest reason why the Toronto Raptors were able to get out to a 22-point lead so quickly was the fact they started the game on fire from beyond the arc. In the first quarter, they shot 10-18 from three, tying a franchise record for threes to open up a game. By the 9:39 mark of the second quarter, Toronto hit their 12th three of the game and started to pull away. However, this would be the last three Toronto would hit until the 2:53 mark of the third quarter. The Raptors missed 11 straight threes in this time and finished the game shooting 16-43 (37.2%).

This is why the comeback Boston made was so incredible. They saw Toronto got off to a blistering start and didn't blink in the face of adversity.

Neemias Queta, for the second year in a row, is one of the most underrated players in the entire NBA. On the season he is now averaging 9.2 points and 6.7 rebounds on 55.6% shooting from the field and 75% from three-point range. In this game, he finished with 11 points, 13 rebounds, and 3 blocks on 2-4 shooting and a team high +27. It's crazy to think that a guy is +27 in 31 minutes in a game where the Celtics were down by 22 points at one point, but that's how good Queta was.

With under a minute to go in the fourth quarter, Queta made up for a turnover on the play before with a dunk to cut the Celtics deficit to 1. After Tatum hit two free throws, Queta played some incredible defense on RJ Barrett who went up for a layup, deterring the shot and hitting two clutch free throws to give the Celtics a 3-point lead. He picked up another block at the final buzzer, capping off one of the best wins of the Celtics season. Queta has continued to impress for the Celtics this season and is creeping his way up the ladder of the best centers in the NBA.

Entering this game, Derrick White was having a similar season to last year where the defense was elite but the three-point shooting wasn't there, only shooting 32.1% from beyond the arc. However, White played arguably the best game of his season against the Raptors, finishing with 19 points, 7 assists, and 4 blocks while shooting 7-15 from the field, 3-7 from three, and finishing as a +18 on the night.

The biggest difference between White's performance in this game versus the rest of the season was the fact that he looked incredibly confident in his shot again. White had 10 of his points in the second half including 7 points in the third quarter and a big three in the fourth quarter that kept the Celtics in the game while Tatum was on the bench.

White's defense was just as impressive. Entering this game, he had 5 blocks on the season as a whole and almost matched that total in one game. It was incredible seeing him show flashes of his Celtics prime again and I hope this can start a stretch of games where White can shoot the ball with confidence. Boston is already an elite offense but if they can get White shooting it at an elite clip again, it's going to be scary for the league.

One of the best parts about the Celtics comeback in this game was the incredible defense Boston played in this game. The Celtics were incredible when it came to protecting the paint, finishing the game with an insane 10 blocks as a team. White had 4, Queta had 3, Tatum had 2, and Scheierman had 1 but this was a testament to how great the Celtics were at not allowing the Raptors to get to the basket. Inside the painted area, Toronto shot 13-34 (38.2%) while at the basket specifically they shot 8-19 (42.1%). When Toronto stopped shooting like the best team of all time, the paint protection allowed Boston to get back into the game and eventually take the win.

The last time the Celtics played a game without Paul George was when they lost to the Houston Rockets on November 2nd. That game was also on the back end of a back-to-back and one of the biggest reasons they lost that game was the fact Boston wasn't able to compete in the minutes when Tatum was on the bench. Payton Pritchard and Derrick White had poor games and with George out, the game got completely out of hand at the start of the fourth quarter, leading to Boston's loss.

In this matchup against the Raptors however, it was a different story. In the minutes when Tatum was on the bench to begin the fourth quarter, the Celtics scored 8 points on 3-5 shooting from the field and 2-3 shooting from three. They were able to outscore Toronto in these minutes but it wasn't all perfect, as they turned the ball over 4 times leading to some wide open shots that the Raptors just didn't knock down. It wasn't a perfect showing from the bench by any means, however I thought they looked a lot more comfortable than they did in Houston. I would still like to see Pritchard and White take over a little more in these scenarios, but it was a fine showing.

Another guy that doesn't get talked about enough for the Celtics is Baylor Scheierman. He got the start in this game and played pretty well, finishing with 11 points and 5 rebounds on 4-9 shooting from the field and 3-6 shooting from three. One thing he does that is different from the rest of the young group of wings the Celtics have is that he is a legitimate threat on the offensive side of the ball alongside his good defense.

This was seen in the Celtics second quarter run after Jayson Tatum drew a flagrant foul. Tatum received the ball on the inbounds pass on the block and found Scheierman on a cross-court pass for a no-dip three. Derrick White then got a steal, leading to a fast break where Tatum threw a behind the back pass to Scheierman who then found a cutting White for the layup. This one sequence shows why Scheierman is so important to Boston. I honestly think he should continue running with lineups alongside Jayson Tatum since Boston has a net rating of +12.2 when the two of them share the court. Scheierman's contributions might not show up in the final box score, but he has a feel for the game that is unmatched and I can't wait to see how he performs if given more minutes to show it.

Although Queta and Tatum had the big plays to end the game for the Celtics, one play that shouldn't get overlooked is the steal by Sam Hauser that gave Boston a chance to put the game out of reach. In a 96-93 game with 15.1 seconds to go, the Raptors threw an inbound pass across the court. Much like a defensive back, Hauser anticipated this pass from the jump, intercepting it and getting fouled, leading to him shooting and making his first two free throws of the season.

Hauser's impact on this game was big, finishing with 8 points and grabbing 9 rebounds alongside 2 steals. He was fighting on the boards with 3 offensive rebounds that gave the Celtics second chances on offense. I wanted to highlight this play because I feel like it will get lost in the shuffle and it is almost a highlight on Hauser's role with the Celtics this season. Sam Hauser has continued to be the steady hand for the Boston Celtics off the bench this season and has looked a lot better than last season when he had a noticeable back injury.

One of my biggest pet peeves when it comes to the NBA is the fact that the schedule makers try their hardest to make the least sense possible. I'm not sure if they had ChatGPT make the schedule this year or something, but it has been awful.

The Celtics are coming off playing one of the most highly anticipated games of the season against the 76ers in Philadelphia. Not only should that game have been in Boston, but what is the reasoning for scheduling a game in Toronto right after? The worst part is, after this game, the Celtics don't play again until Sunday night against the Dallas Mavericks. It doesn't end there; after the Mavericks game, they play ANOTHER back-to-back against the Magic on Monday.

What is the point of playing a back-to-back and then getting three days off just to play another back-to-back? Why do we have to miss out on a weekend of Celtics basketball? The NBA is wondering why they have so many injuries and then schedule games like this. What are we doing here?

#2709. NFL Draft stock report: Buy- Sammy Omosigho, LB, UCLA

Everyone first associates Los Angeles with the film industry, but it has a storied history as an elite sports city, which is why L.A. will host the summer olympics, again, in 2028.

The City of Angels boasts the basketball team with the most glorious history on both the college and NBA level. Not to mention the richest and most powerful Major League Baseball team.

When it comes to college football, the UCLA Bruins are defying all odds and expectations, as they sit undefeated with just three regular season games to play.

Much like L.A. produces timeless pop culture products across numerous genres, this UCLA team can beat you in numerous ways. The Bruins have stars in every position group, with Sammy Omosigho standing out in the linebacking corps. Omosigho and the Bruins take on the Illinois Fighting Illini, in a Friday night primetime affair, nationally televised on FOX.

It will be interesting to see how Illini Offensive Coordinator Barry Lunney gameplans against the Bruins defense, which is led by Omosigho who was named a semifinalist for the Walter Camp Player of the Year award. The award honors the best overall player, regardless of position. In its 60 years of existence, only three defenders have ever claimed the award, so Omosigho has work cut out for him.

But he certainly has the stats on his side: 61 tackles, 5.5 sacks, four passes defensed and an NCAA-leading five forced fumbles. He simply makes plays, and that's gotten him on the NFL Draft radar this season. He currently projects as a high fourth-round to low sixth-round prospect, but his draft stock has been on a positive trajectory all season long.

#2707. Opponent Breakdown: North Carolina Tar Heels Defense

Defense is Bill Belichick's forte, and the North Carolina Tar Heels are benefiting from his expertise this year. For the second straight year, Belichick has his defense ranked in the top 50 in yards per play. His group is being led by his son Brian after his son Steve left the team earlier this season. While the defense has taken a step back this year, they have played well enough to keep the Tar Heels in each game, and they've made big plays at big moments.

The most talented group on this team is the defensive line, with a couple of NFL prospects. Melkart Abou Jaoude is the returning ACC leader in sacks, while Jaylen Harvey has been a very good addition from Penn State with 21 pressures this season. The edges of this defense haven't put up crazy numbers from a havoc standpoint, but they will be key players for this defense if Louisville continues to attack the edges of the defense.

The interior of the line is where this defense is at its best. Xavier Lewis is one of the best defensive tackles in the country. He is in the top five in pressures, tackles for loss, and sacks among his position group. The 6-0/260 tackle is extremely undersized, but he is very quick, and he uses his quickness to beat blocks to get into the backfield. He will be a key player in this game and will likely cause some issues for Louisville's offensive line.

Isaiah Johnson and Leroy Jackson are the other top players on the interior of the defense. Jackson has 14 pressures on the season as the main backup for Lewis, but he and Johnson provide really good size on the inside as well. Johnson is big enough to demand a double team, which has been a factor in Lewis' big season. He has been able to get one-on-one matchups often, and that has not gone well for offensive linemen.

UNC's linebackers have benefited more than just about anyone from the strong play of the defensive line. Derek McDonald and Peyton Sheelmann are averaging 19 tackles a game between the two of them. Both players are ranked in the top 25 in tackles nationally, and they are constantly running free when you watch their games. Louisville has adapted their running game over the last few weeks, but they will likely have a hard time running the stretch zone runs that they really like. These two guys can run, and they will have a lot of space to get downhill to make tackles behind the line.

Jaiden Patterson leads a solid cornerback group that has played at an average level this season. UNC has given up a lot of yardage this season, but they are better when it comes to metrics like passer rating. The corners have had some issues against the top players they've seen this year. Umari Hatcher, Jordon Faison, Calvin Russell, and Bryant Wesco all stood out to me when I watched their games. Those receivers were able to get open and make big plays on the outside.

The biggest playmaker outside of the defensive linemen is Greg Smith at free safety. He leads the team with 3 interceptions this year, and he's at his best as a deep safety playing center field. Smith can also come down into the box in run support or cover if needed. He's having one of the best seasons in the ACC at safety. While this secondary isn't great, they do have a couple of players who can make a play on the ball, which is not something I would say about the last few opponents for the Cards.

#2706. Has Kingston Flemings already arrived?

It's a common refrain that the jump to the NBA is hardest for young point guards. With how fast the game is, the high level of skill, and the physicality that seasoned veterans possess, quick adaptation to the level of competition is incredibly difficult.

Kingston Flemings bucked one similar trend in his lone collegiate season playing for Kelvin Sampson at Houston. Sampson is famous for tempering expectations for his young guards, often having them to wait until their upperclassmen to carve out big roles for his team.

Instead, all Flemings did was start all 37 games and play 31.7 minutes per contest in his one-and-done season there despite arriving on campus as a fresh faced 18-year-old.

Now, as a rookie for the Atlanta Hawks, the no. 8 overall pick became a starter in just his eighth career NBA game.

Predictably, there appeared to be a bit of nerves and discomfort throughout the first four games of his professional career. He seemed hesitant to attack and deferred to the veterans on the team whenever possible.

Again, not a surprise for a 19-year-old guard on the big stage.

At the same time, 35-year-old CJ McCollum has shown signs of slowing down this season. He's never been a particularly willing passer as the team's quasi-point guard, and the numerous slow starts (both from McCollum personally and the team at large) in the first few games became an immediate worry.

But something clicked after that — and Quin Snyder felt the time was right to make the lineup change for the good of the team, although admittedly the public comments have largely been through the frame of CJ McCollum asking to come off the bench in some respects.

"CJ [McCollum] and I, I respect him," Snyder had to say prior to the home game against the Wizards. "We've known each other a long time. He respects me. A lot of dialogue between the two of us generally about our team. That includes film. Just looking at our team, we had a couple of tough starts. It certainly wasn't attributable to any one thing. It felt like as we looked at what was there, there was something that we could do differently. Potentially help him be impactful with the bench group. Which he did. And also give our starters a different look to get them going."

In Flemings' first four games, he was just 6-for-18 (33%) from the field including 1-for-5 (20%) from three and only got to the free throw line once (missing that attempt). He's also someone who values the ball a ton, and so his 17-to-11 (1.54:1) assist-to-turnover ratio must have come as a disappointment.

This tepidness was on full display — clearly not wanting to make mistakes — and as a result playing less freely than one should or could.

But over the next seven games, he has come alive to the tune of 32-for-55 (58%) from the field, 8-of-16 (50%) from three, 10 free throw attempts, and 31 assists to just 14 turnovers (2.1:1 assist-to-turnover ratio).

Flemings' lightning quick first step can be relied upon to create early advantages, and his high release point has helped him get his jump shot off against defenders of all size:

And now, he's leveraging his scoring pressure into playmaking for others and relocating for better shots if defenses play him too aggressively. Three-point shooting was thought to be a weakness of his coming into the 2026 NBA Draft, but so far he's hit 5-of-9 (55.6%) of his catch-and-shoot three-point attempts and 43% of all three-point attempts (9-for-21).

Flemings is a careful, efficient playmaker who avoids turnovers at a high level for someone in his age bracket. He's flashed good vision to poke holes in the defense and to get the ball out of his hands to his teammates in space. Here, he splits the Cavaliers 2-3 zone with a quick skip pass and a helpful Lu Dort hammer screen:

In fact, thus far into the season, Flemings is tops on the Hawks in potential assists per 36 minutes (13.0), narrowly eclipsing Jalen Johnson (12.2) and Dyson Daniels (11.8). He's doing this while averaging the most turnovers per 36 minutes on the team (3.7), so there's still room for growth, but it's been refreshing to see him not hesitate after making mistakes.

Defensively, the first thing you notice is his level of compete against players 6-foot and 7-foot tall alike. Here, he helps and crashes down on Giannis Antetokounmpo ready to lay the ball up in the dunker's spot:

And it's not just flashy disruptive plays, either. The great Steph Noh detailed Flemings' penchant for just doing the defensive basics: a high motor, making the right rotations and being in the right position, and holding his own against bigger players.

Flemings is a different breed of point guard. He can run a pick-and-roll if you need to. He can set screens and cut if you need him to. He can spot up and wait for a swing-swing if you need him to. He doesn't take breaks on defense. And most importantly, he isn't a target for opposing offenses to pick on.

He's a player that truly wants to impact the game in more ways than scoring — and the scoring has even been efficient (60% true shooting as of November 10)!

But with the Hawks looking to pressure the ball on defense and create transition opportunities off turnovers, Flemings fits neatly into that new ethos. So, his arrival just may coincide with a new Hawks identity that few teams want to see in a 48-minute grind of a basketball game.
